pr_title: Handle expired tokens in cluster migration tests
pr_body:
This PR addresses a failure around token BWC during cluster upgrade
tests: the tests assert that tokens created in a cluster before (or
during) an upgrade are still valid in the mixed or upgraded clusters.
Our cluster upgrade test suites are long running however such that
tokens created in the old (or mixed) cluster may be expired by the time
we test their validity. The maximum lifetime of tokens is configured
via a setting which has a max value of 1h. This PR extends the lifetime
of all tokens by writing to the `.security-tokens` index directly, for
each test where this is necessary. This (hacky) solution allows us to
robustly exercise the target path of the test (validating that a token
is valid and authenticates correctly) while keeping the fix confined to
test code (as opposed to solving this via a system property).

Closes #77350

This might be due to the rolling upgrade test procedure which I'm not totally familiar with. I don't know how good the reproduction line is supposed to work here, adding it just in case.

This failed again today: 
* https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/vnrpri3dk6vzy
* https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/b7sjtskv6sdhm

Test that failed because of expired token: 
* UpgradeClusterClientYamlTestSuiteIT » test {p0=upgraded_cluster/50_token_auth/Get the indexed token and use if to authenticate}
* TokenBackwardsCompatibilityIT » testAccessTokensWorkInUpgradedCluster

When trying to reproduce the `testAccessTokensWorkInUpgradedCluster` failure I ran into the same issue that @cbuescher mentioned. The test failed, but not because expired token but because of `index_not_found_exception`. See: https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/ieeibaketyhbq 

Not that this does seem to be failing regularly. The `TokenBackwardsCompatibilityIT#testAccessTokensWorkInUpgradedCluster()` failed 7 times in the last week.

Based on @slobodanadamovic's [comment](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/88988#issuecomment-1202318756):

The root cause analysis that the token from the legacy cluster is expired by the time we get to this test makes sense to me. Thinking about the following:

We are planning to drop BWC support for pre-7.17 tokens altogether (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/87726). Since 7.17 tokens will still be supported this might not help us here. I haven't dug into the test setup yet but if this helps us cut down on the overall number of tests that need to run and therefore on test duration and cluster age, we might just naturally end up below the 1 hour mark again. This ofc doesn't really address the root cause but still felt worth mentioning. 

In terms of more immediate fixes I'm wondering if we should simply account for token age in the test: based on either token or cluster age, determine if the token _should_ still be valid or if we expect it to be expired and assert accordingly. To keep things simple, we could even just add an `assumeTrue` that skips the test altogether if the cluster (or token) is too old. ~I think the source we fetch for the token includes expiration, so we should be able to check if we expect it to be valid or not.~ <- not true, we only store the actual token values, not the whole doc.  

One more alternative would be to refresh tokens periodically, though that seems overly complex at first glance.

Hmm it looks like the reason it doesn't reproduce locally and fails with an `index_not_found` instead, is that the test relies on other tests to create tokens (since those need to be created in the old cluster). `storeTokens` is what creates the relevant index and populates it with tokens, and that method is not called on setup or in the specific failing test (`testAccessTokensWorkInUpgradedCluster` in my case).

It seems concerning that these tests took so long to run. The entire suite finishes/fails around 4 hours. The gap between running oldClusterTest and upgradedClusterTest is more than 1 hour. I noticed they are all of job `elastic+elasticsearch+main+multijob+platform-support-unix` for different OSes. Is this normal? @mark-vieira

Based [on gradle performance stats](https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/scans/performance?performance.metric=buildTime&performance.offset=4973&performance.pageSize=172&search.buildOutcome=success&search.relativeStartTime=P28D&search.rootProjectNames=elasticsearch&search.tags=elastic%2Belasticsearch%2Bmain%2Bmultijob%2Bplatform-support-unix&search.tasks=check&search.timeZoneId=Europe/Berlin#performance.focusedBuild=hguh5mpeprzzo) for the `check` task and label `elastic+elasticsearch+main+multijob+platform-support-unix`, the overall build time does not appear to have changed over the past 28 days. The average is 4 hr 15 min for successful builds.

It is a little suspect that there would be such a long time between `oldClusterTest` and `upgradedClusterTest`, though that also seems consistent with the past since the same issue--at least so far as I can tell--was occurring already back in Sep '21. 

My guess for why there is such a big gap is that we first run multiple test suites with `oldClusterTest` in a batch, then mixed, then upgraded. However, that's mere surmise on my part. Will wait for Mark to confirm or deny!

> My guess for why there is such a big gap is that we first run multiple test suites with oldClusterTest in a batch, then mixed, then upgraded. However, that's mere surmise on my part. Will wait for Mark to confirm or deny!

This is accurate. Our mixed cluster tests are by far the slowest running tests in the suite. I've raised several issues about this in the past. The general finding is that mixed clusters, especially with older 6.x nodes, perform _much_ worse. I can't speculate as to why that is but that's the story being told by our test suites. In practice mixed clusters are a transietn situation, so I think from a performance standpoint, this isn't a real priority. Of course for our test suites it's a different story.

So yes, they are incredibly slow, and yes, we are aware, and no, there's not a whole lot we can do about it other than potentially split up the test suites or run more in parallel but their are complex obstacles to doing so.
